notes: Company is German (HQ Hannover); checked both the German storefront connox.de (hreflang x-default, channel 100001) and the English mirror connox.com (channel 100005). NAVIGATION CHECKED: full mega-menu, footer, sitemap.xml (8 sub-sitemaps, ~14.5k URLs grepped for outlet|restposten|raeumung|ausverkauf - no matches), robots.txt (no Claude disallow). Neither locale has a nav item or URL literally named Clearance/Outlet/Restposten/Raeumung/Endverkauf/Last Chance. Both locales do have one nav item labelled plainly 'SALE' (same English word used even on the German site: https://www.connox.de/design-angebote.html, h1 'Sale') - this is Connox's one discount-merchandising listing. Rendered with Playwright (category pages are 100% client-side React, static HTML is an empty mount point): it is a real PLP - 7573 items on connox.de / 7634 items on connox.com, every tile showing an RRP struck through against a lower sale price with a -XX% badge, default-filtered isOffer=true against the site's underlying items API (categoryId=100935&isOffer=true), default sort 'Most popular'. This is the ambiguous Sale-vs-Clearance case flagged by the brief: on one hand it is a very large, evergreen, catalogue-wide percent-off listing with a generic 'Sale' label and no on-page outlet/clearance/discontinued/permanent-markdown copy visible anywhere on the rendered page (checked for discontinued/Auslaufmodell/Sonderposten/permanent/dauerhaft/clearance - none found) - which per the brief's own test points toward a generic promotional Sale, not Clearance. On the other hand the English version's <meta og:description> (site-authored, though not user-visible copy) explicitly reads 'Find attractive offers, bargains and discontinued lines from our interior design shop', i.e. the site itself describes the listing as including discontinued/end-of-line stock alongside ordinary discounts - a genuine (if partial) permanence signal. Given this genuine mixed signal, recording the row per the brief's 'if uncertain, still record and flag' instruction rather than silently excluding or silently including. Reported using the German storefront (connox.de) as primary scope since it is this German company's native/default site (x-default) and the counts are consistent across both locales (7573 vs 7634, same underlying category/filter structure) confirming it is the same listing concept, not a locale-specific anomaly.

rows.flag: MANUAL REVIEW: AMBIGUOUS SALE/CLEARANCE - page and nav are labelled plainly 'Sale' (English word, used even on the German-language site) with default sort 'Most popular' and no on-page outlet/clearance/discontinued wording, which reads like a generic catalogue-wide promotional sale rather than a curated permanent-clearance/outlet section; however the site's own English meta description for this exact page explicitly says it includes 'discontinued lines' alongside ordinary offers/bargains, so it may partially represent genuine end-of-line clearance stock merged into one large Sale listing. Human should decide whether this qualifies as Clearance for this project or should be dropped as a plain Sale page.
